summary: Checkpoint 1 frontend smoke testing passed on the public Expo preview at a 375x667 mobile viewport. Home, required-field validation, body-region choices, generated patient ID, local save confirmation, return navigation, offline count refresh, prohibited-claims check, and horizontal overflow checks were exercised.
action_items: Consider adding explicit testID attributes to Patient Details inputs, back button, sex chips, and body-region chips for robust automated coverage; current controls are accessible by placeholder/label/text selectors.
critical_code_review_comments: The requested checkpoint behavior is implemented without backend or mocked API dependencies.

savePatient errors are represented by a boolean, but an unexpected storage rejection from getPatients/setItem would escape handleContinue rather than reaching storageError; consider a try/catch in a later hardening pass.
seed_data_creation: One test patient was saved locally in the browser preview storage during the smoke test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The first save test generated an OA-YYYYMMDD-XXXX patient ID and showed local confirmation. A duplicate mounted home node appeared transiently after router.replace; this was a selector strictness artifact, not a functional failure. A fresh run showed one home node, correct count behavior, usable back navigation, and no horizontal overflow.
rca_of_issue: No functional issue reproduced. The only automation failure was waiting on a strict home-screen selector while two transient route nodes existed after replace; using a count/visible-node assertion resolved it.
